_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Armenia covering Urartu, Orontid dynasty, Artaxiad empire (Tigranes the Great), Arsacid Armenia and first Christian state (AD 301), Bagratid kingdom, Armenian renaissance, Seljuk/Mongol invasions, Safavid-Ottoman partition, Armenian Genocide 1915, First Republic 1918, Soviet Armenia, Nagorno-Karabakh conflict, independence 1991, and 2020/2023 Artsakh losses.

religion.note: First nation to adopt Christianity as state religion (AD 301); Armenian Apostolic Church is autocephalous Oriental Orthodox

ethnic_groups.name: Armenian
ethnic_groups.notes: Indo-European; unique alphabet (Mesrop Mashtots, AD 405); diaspora ~7 million worldwide (more than homeland population); Genocide survivors' descendants

ethnic_groups.name: Yezidi (Kurdish)
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest minority; Aragatsotn and Armavir regions; Yezidi religion; Kurdish-speaking; distinct from Muslim Kurds

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Assyrian, Greek, Ukrainian, Kurdish Muslim)
ethnic_groups.notes: Small Assyrian community; historically Greek community; post-2020 Artsakh Armenian refugees (~100,000) from Nagorno-Karabakh

geography.terrain: Armenian Highland; volcanic plateau with mountains; rapid elevation changes; Lake Sevan at 1,900 m
geography.notes: Landlocked South Caucasus country; Mount Ararat (cultural symbol) lies across Turkish border; seismic zone (devastating 1988 Spitak earthquake).

economy_extended.notes: Post-2022 boom from Russian capital/talent influx; IT sector growing rapidly (10%+ of GDP); mining (copper, gold, molybdenum); blockaded by Turkey/Azerbaijan; diaspora remittances 10%+ of GDP.

health.notes: Soviet-era healthcare infrastructure; high physician density but uneven quality; out-of-pocket costs ~80% of health spending; universal coverage aspiration but significant gaps.

food_agriculture.notes: Armenian brandy (Ararat) internationally renowned; apricot believed to have originated here (Prunus armeniaca); wine production reviving from ancient tradition (6,100-year-old Areni-1 winery).

energy.notes: Metsamor nuclear plant (Soviet-era VVER-440) provides ~34% of electricity; considered seismic risk; Russian gas dependency; Iran-Armenia gas pipeline; 500 MW solar potential being developed.

transport.notes: Landlocked with closed borders with Turkey and Azerbaijan; transit via Georgia and Iran; Zvartnots International Airport (Yerevan) main gateway; Soviet-era rail system; North-South Highway Corridor under construction.

tourism.notes: Diaspora tourism significant; first country to adopt Christianity (301 AD); wine tourism growing (world's oldest winery at Areni); 2022+ Russian visitors surged post-invasion.

legal_system.notes: 2015 constitutional reform shifted to parliamentary system; judicial independence improving but corruption concerns remain; Constitutional Court reformed 2020.

human_rights_gender.notes: 2018 Velvet Revolution improved democratic prospects; gender-based violence remains concern; strong sex-ratio imbalance at birth (son preference); LGBTQ+ community faces social stigma.

security_stability.notes: 2020 Nagorno-Karabakh war lost to Azerbaijan; 2023 Azerbaijan takeover of Artsakh displaced 100,000+ ethnic Armenians; ongoing border tensions; Russian peacekeepers unreliable.

unesco_intangible_heritage: Armenian letter art and cultural expressions
Performance of Armenian epic 'Daredevils of Sassoun'
world_heritage_sites_list: Cathedral and Churches of Echmiatsin and the Archaeological Site of Zvartnots
Monastery of Geghard and Upper Azat Valley
cultural_heritage.notes: First nation to adopt Christianity (301 AD); Armenian alphabet created by Mesrop Mashtots (405 AD); genocide of 1915 central to national identity; massive global diaspora.

comparative_rankings.notes: Rapid rise in ease of doing business and competitiveness; IT sector becoming regional hub; post-Velvet Revolution democratic improvements.
comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: Nikol Pashinyan
current_leader.title: Prime Minister (head of government)
current_leader.notes: Civil Contract party; came to power via 2018 Velvet Revolution; lost 2020 Nagorno-Karabakh war to Azerbaijan; Artsakh fell September 2023; peace negotiations with Baku ongoing

former_leaders.name: Levon Ter-Petrosyan
former_leaders.notes: First president; ANM; Karabakh war victor; resigned under pressure over Karabakh compromise proposal

former_leaders.name: Robert Kocharyan
former_leaders.notes: From Karabakh; hardliner; economic growth; March 2008 crackdown on protests

former_leaders.name: Serzh Sargsyan
former_leaders.notes: Republican Party; tried to continue as PM after constitutional change; ousted by Pashinyan's Velvet Revolution 2018
